decisions.issues: Acceptable, with one small continuity flaw worth a retouch. Seen at full zoom, the brand on the inner LEFT forearm is a pale patch made of small rings with a few radiating lines, a bit like a beetle. It is not letters, a cross or a crescent, and at reading size it is only a faint pale smudge. The long white scar starts near the elbow and runs onto the inner upper arm, not from the wrist toward the elbow. Everything else matches. Kayal is a bay with a black mane and black lower legs and no white markings, in a leather headstall with brass buckles and a rope lead. She pushes her muzzle into his cupped empty palms. Nagoji is bare-chested in a cream mundu and shoulder cloth, with a topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold ear stud, silver chain and the ivory conch knife at his waist. The stable, laterite wall, hanging brass lamp with open wicks and dusk sky match 7.1 and 7.2. The hands are sound and there is no painted text. Lettering: one balloon in the dusk sky right of his head (x 0.80 to 0.98, y 0.08 to 0.32), the other over the roof beams at upper left (x 0.03 to 0.38, y 0.02 to 0.18), clear of the lamp, his face and the hands.

Acceptable. Minor only: Nagoji's jaw has a faint skin texture that disappears at reading size and does not read as a beard. Revathi's front hair is curlier than in 7.2, but the long jasmine braid falls down the front of her sari as it does there. The beat reads clearly. Revathi smiles genuinely at Nagoji, chin on her hand, both leaning on the rail. Two small nieces run past and bicker at right, one clutching a small brass object. Nagoji has his topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny flush gold ear stud, silver chain, bare chest with the cream shoulder cloth and the ivory conch knife at his waist, as in 7.1 and 7.3. Revathi wears the indigo-and-gold sari, the long flat-coin necklace and no second chain or tali, with jhumkas, gold armlets and bangles, the sandalwood line and grey threads. Kayal has no white markings and wears the leather headstall with brass buckles. The stable, lamp and dusk light match the page, the hands are sound and there is no painted text. Lettering: both Revathi balloons go in the dusk sky at upper right (x 0.70 to 0.98, y 0.0 to 0.28), clear of the lamp, her head and the children, with tails down to her mouth.

Minor only. The tight framing crops Revathi's face at the eyes, which suits a tight knot-tying shot but means her sandalwood hairline mark is out of frame. Her hair at the nape reads as loose curls with jasmine rather than a neatly coiled, pinned bun. Nagoji's silver chain of office is not visible under the shoulder cloth. His identity matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, grey at the temples, topknot cut by the top edge, plain white cloth with no gold border and no knife. Both hands are anatomically sound and pinch the yellow thread and gold pendant at the knot, so the beat reads clearly. There is no painted text. The upper-right sky, roofline and plain courtyard wall give clear space for the long off-panel PRIEST balloon, with its tail toward the right edge where the priest sits beyond the fire.

Acceptable with minor deviations. Nagoji has his silver chain of office missing, and the brand on his left forearm cannot be seen. Ramayyan sits further along the same row of leaves rather than directly across it. Revathi's tali is a gold pendant on a thin gold-yellow cord: it sits high at her throat and is clearly separate from the long bead necklace, but it is not obviously a yellow thread. Her sandalwood hairline mark is not visible, only a small bindi. Lettering space is tight because heads reach high in the strip. Usable low-detail areas are: the dusk sky band across the top 10 to 15 percent; the wall and sky gap between Nagoji and Padmini (x about 0.41 to 0.49); the wall between Revathi and Nagoji (x about 0.21 to 0.29, y 0.15 to 0.30); and the tiled roof above Ramayyan (x 0.75 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.15). Everything else is right. Nagoji has a thick moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a small gold ear stud, a topknot and a plain white mundu with no knife. Revathi sits on his right and Padmini on his left, leaning in, in her finest white with jasmine. Ramayyan is thin and balding in plain white, eating with his fingers without looking up. Banana leaves, rice, pappadam, brass tumblers, steaming avial carried by a server whose face is cropped out, and brass oil lamps at evening all match the script. The art has no painted text, hands are sound, and there are no doubles of any principal.
